html:
SMTO-SKL-0103 — That Microsoft 365 request is too large

GUID: 3dcd9052-f52c-5577-a698-7c6f299ab46d
Slug: microsoft365-result-limit-exceeded
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • SMTO has size limits for Microsoft 365 requests. This one asked for too many results, too many people, or too big a file, so SMTO stopped it.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. For lists and searches, ask for 100 items or fewer at a time, and ask for the next page when you need more. SMTO returns at most 100 items per page.
  2. When checking when people are free, ask about 20 people or fewer at a time. Free and busy checks can cover at most 20 people in one request.
  3. For files, use files of 250 MB or less, or narrow your search with a folder, sender or date range. Very large files and very large replies are over SMTO's limits.

What success looks like

  • The Agent returns results or finishes the transfer without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and mention what you were asking for.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A microsoft365 size limit was hit: a JSON response over 2 MiB, a page limit outside 1-100, a file over 250 MiB, or a calendar_availability request for more than 20 schedules.

What this means

  • A response exceeds the JSON byte bound, a page limit is outside 1–100, file bytes exceed their bound, or availability requests exceed 20 schedules. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A response exceeds the JSON byte bound, a page limit is outside 1–100, file bytes exceed their bound, or availability requests exceed 20 schedules.

How to diagnose it

  • Identify the exceeded bound instead of applying a file-size fix to a JSON/page/schedule limit.

How to fix it

  • Reduce the scope to the documented bounds: limit between 1 and 100 per page (continue with cursor), at most 20 schedules per calendar_availability call, files and downloads up to 250 MiB, and narrower filters or $select-sized results so a single Graph response stays under 2 MiB.
  • Reduce the named JSON, page, schedule-count or transfer scope to its supported bound.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • A deliberately narrowed operation fits its specific response or transfer limit.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
